title.narrative: KtK- Advancing the role of women as agents for peace and development – Phase II
KtK- Att främja kvinnors roll som agenter för fred och utveckling - Fas II

description.narrative:
Kvinna Till Kvinna lämnade in ett projektförslag för att begära 30 000 000 SEK för att genomföra "Framtagande av kvinnors roll som agenter för fred och utveckling - Fas II". Aktivitetsperioden är från 01.01.2022-31.12.2023. Sida har tidigare stött genomförandet av KtK:s regionala MENA- och Syrien-program 2017-2021.
Kvinna till Kvinna kommer att vidarebefordra runt 55 % av stödet till sina lokala partners i och utanför Syrien att genomföra deras verksamhet inom olika tematiska områden men med fokus på jämställdhet och kvinnors rättigheter. Insatsen innefattar också mycket stöd till kapacitetsutveckling, både tematisk och organisatorisk samt fokus på påverkansarbete inom FN Resolutionen 1325.

Kvinna Till Kvinna submitted a project proposal to request for 30 000 000 SEK to implement "Advancing the role of women as agents for peace and development-Phase II". The activity period is from 01.01.2022-31.12.2023. Sida has previously supported the implementation of the KtK regional MENA and Syria programme from 2017-2021.
Kvinna till Kvinna will pass on around 55% of the support to its local partners inside and outside Syria to carry out their activities in various thematic areas, but with a focus on gender equality and women's rights. The effort also includes a lot of support for capacity development, both thematically and organizationally, as well as a focus on advocacy work within UN Resolution 1325.

The overall objective of the intervention is to Strengthen Kvinna till Kvinna Partner Organisations (POs) organisational and technical capacities to increase women's political and economic participation, protect women and girls from GBV, and strengthening of gender discourse in Syria. The specific objectives of the intervention that are intended to be achieved at the end of the intervention are the following:
- Partner Organizations have increased capacity to operate effectively and sustainability.
- Partner Organizations have contributed to increase women's participation as actors of change in the targeted geographic areas in Syria.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
The following are the most significant results that this project has achieved, as reported in the Final Report 2022-2024. The economic instability, insecurity, and post-earthquake physical and mental trauma are all important factors to keep in mind when assessing these results:
According to the external evaluation, the program has effectively amplified women's voices within diverse platforms in Syria, indicating a significant impact on gender mainstreaming and conflict resolution.
Between 2022-2024 Kvinna till Kvinnas partner organizations (POs) directly reached approximately 5,300 rightsholders (90% women and 10% men) and indirectly engaged over 49,000 individuals through initiatives and social media campaigns. About 2/3 (62%) of participants reported increased knowledge on human rights, peacebuilding, participation, gender, and womens rights topics.
Through targeted activies and community initiatives, the POs fostered an environment that promotes and supports women's involvement and participation in decision-making at the community level, with 2,918 community members (men and women) engaged.
1,456 women and girls were reached with protection services. Less than half (46.5%) of women and girls who benefitted from protection services reported a positive change (behaviours, PSS wellbeing, the capacity to cope).
1,350 women participated in women's economic empowerment activities which included education and vocational empowerment and social media campagings that challenged stereotypes and perceptions, highlighting women as agents of change and progress in society. While only 18 participating women reportedly secured employment in areas such as journalism, project management and civil society, many others were able to sell products that they created at home such as clothes.
KtK's POs made important and significant contributions to strengthening the gender discourse in Syria. Badael created and developed an oral history digital archive, which houses 247 oral history interviews with Syrian women in Turkey. The Syrian Female Journalist Network (SFJN9) supported Syrian media institutions in promoting gender-sensitive discourse and behavior, and in addressing the lack of Syrian women experts in media coverage. By working with media actors, the project contributed to increased gender-senstive content, improving women's representation and expanding coverage of women's rights issues.
One of KtK's POs produced a film The Visual Feminist Manifesto, which was premiered at the Rotterdam International Film Festival where it was selected for the "Bright Future" category and received the Youth Jury Award. The film, based on 90 interviews with Syrian women, challenges and redefines societal norms and patriarchy within the context of Syria, Lebanon, Jordan and Palestine.
KtK strengthened the capacity of 7 POs through individualized needs inventories and capacity building plans. Depending on the needs assessed in the inventories, POs were strengthened in terms of taxation, legal and compliance affairs, human resource policies, strategies and skills, feminist management and communication, procurement systems and digitalization, fundraising, outreach and networking and duty of care. Nearly all (95%) of surveyed reported that improved structures were contributing to the sustainability of the organisation
KtK's partners' thematic capacities were strengthened in the areas of justice, peacebuilding and gender, women's economic empowerment, strengthening gender discourse, gender-based violoence, feminist economic approaches and others.
KtK's partners advocacy efforts were amplified outside of Syria through participation in global dialogues (ie at AWID International Conference and the 8th Brussels Conference on Syria, together with the Embassy), and thorugh networking with other feminists in the MENA region.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
